comment: Which words are everyday words of the user's languages, answered with the system's spelling dictionaries (ADR-DESK-038, amended 2026-11-04). `dictionaries`: which of a system's dictionaries (`available`, as the macOS and Windows spell checkers name theirs) serves each of the user's languages. `known`: the Linux answer, from the Hunspell files in `hunspell/` (made up for these tests; en_US has an affix rule, el_GR's is ISO 8859-7, pt_BR's names no encoding and is ISO 8859-1, ru's and th's name their encodings as Hunspell's own aliases, xx's names one not known, yy has no .aff). The app sends words in lowercase; `known` lists them as given, in the order asked.

dictionaries.name: else the first of the language by name
names and tags match whatever their case and separator
a script is skipped and a numeric region matched
a POSIX locale's encoding is ignored, and a tag naming no language is no language without a dictionary
each dictionary once, in the languages' order
a language none serves is unavailable

known.name: an everyday word is known, a made-up name is not
a word an affix rule makes is known
a name the dictionary keeps capitalized is not known in lowercase
the language's region picks its dictionary
a word of another language is not known without its dictionary
a dictionary in another encoding is read in it
an encoding named by Hunspell's aliases for Windows Cyrillic and Thai is read in it
a dictionary in an encoding not known serves no language
a dictionary without its .aff is not one
a language without a dictionary knows nothing
